text:
Can you write the pitch for our crowdfunding campaign? I chair the volunteer group trying to reopen the one-screen cinema in our town of 6,500. It closed in 2022.

Facts:
- We need $85,000 to replace the projector and sound system and fix the roof. The building's owner has agreed to rent it to us for $1 a year for 10 years if we raise it.
- We ran a campaign 3 years ago for $120,000. It reached $47,000 and we refunded everyone.
- This time a local bank has pledged $25,000 if we raise the rest by June 30.
- 46 volunteers have signed up to run the box office and the snack bar.
- When it closed, the cinema was selling about 180 tickets a week.
- The nearest other cinema is 38 miles away.

Keep it under 350 words.

Before I draft, a few questions. Your answers will change what the pitch says:

1. **Why did it close in 2022, and what makes it viable now?** Backers who remember the closure will want to know it won't happen again. Does a volunteer-run model with a $1 rent cover running costs at roughly 180 tickets a week?
2. **What's different from the campaign three years ago?** I'd mention it openly, since many of your backers probably gave last time. Did the target drop from $120,000 to $85,000 because the scope changed, or because the lease deal or something else cut costs?
3. **If you fall short, what happens to people's money?** Is this all-or-nothing with refunds again? And to confirm: the deadline is June 30, 2027, and the crowd needs to raise $60,000 to unlock the bank's $25,000?
4. **What do backers get, and is there a typical amount you're hoping for?** For example ticket bundles, a name on a seat, or opening-night passes.
5. **Is there one local story or voice we can use?** For example a longtime projectionist, a family that drives 76 miles round trip for a film, or a target reopening date.

If you don't know some of these, say so and I'll write the pitch without them.

1. I don't know exactly why it closed or whether 180 tickets a week covers running costs.

2. The goal is $35,000 lower than last time, and the bank's $25,000 counts toward it. I'm not sure what changed in the scope.

3. Yes, all-or-nothing. If we don't reach $85,000 by June 30, every pledge is returned in full. Yes, it's June 30, 2027, and we need $60,000 from the public. The campaign opens May 1.

4. Don't know yet.

5. We plan to reopen by Thanksgiving if we raise it. I don't have a personal story to give you.

Ruth Albers, the Majestic on Main Street

<final_document>
**Bring the Majestic Back**

The one screen at the Majestic on Main Street has been dark since 2022. Today, seeing a movie in a theater means a 76-mile round trip.

We can change that by Thanksgiving.

**The deal**

The building's owner has agreed to rent the Majestic to us for $1 a year for ten years. The condition is that we get it ready to open. That takes $85,000 for a new projector, a new sound system and a repaired roof.

A local bank has pledged $25,000 of that. The bank's condition is that the town raises the other $60,000 by June 30.

**Why this time is different**

Some of you backed our campaign three years ago. It reached $47,000 of a $120,000 goal, and we returned every dollar, as we said we would. This campaign works the same way. It's all-or-nothing. If we don't reach $85,000 by June 30, every pledge comes back to you in full.

Three things have changed. The goal is $35,000 lower. A bank has already committed a quarter of it. And there's a ten-year lease waiting for us.

Last time, this town pledged $47,000. This time we need $60,000 from you, which is $13,000 more than you gave before.

**Who will run it**

Forty-six of your neighbors have already signed up to run the box office and the snack bar. In its last days, the Majestic was still selling about 180 tickets a week, so the audience was there right up to the end.

**What we're asking**

Pledge what you can by June 30. If you gave last time, please give again. If you didn't, this is the time. Then tell one person who misses Friday nights on Main Street.

If we reach the goal, the projector goes in, the roof gets fixed, and the lights come back on this Thanksgiving.

Thank you,

Ruth Albers
Chair, the volunteer group working to reopen the Majestic
</final_document>

The pitch is 309 words. A few things to check before May 1:

- **"This Thanksgiving":** this is accurate if the page goes live in 2027. Change it if the text will also be used somewhere else.
- **Reward tiers:** once you've decided on them, add them under "What we're asking." I left them out rather than make them up.
- **Group name:** the sign-off uses a description in place of a name. Put in your group's official name if it has one.
- **The bank:** if it's happy to be named, use its name. A named local bank is more convincing than "a local bank."
- **Running costs:** I didn't claim the Majestic will pay its own way, because you don't know that yet. Expect backers to ask. A short plan for covering running costs once it opens would be the most useful thing to add before launch, even a rough budget showing what $1 rent and volunteer staff save.
